panels.title: CPU by workload
panels.description: CPU usage in cores per workload, summed over the selected nodes and stacked. A pod's workload comes from Prometheus's recording rule namespace_workload_pod:kube_pod_owner:relabel: what owns it, through its ReplicaSet for a Deployment or Rollout. A static pod, or a pod the rule doesn't know, shows under its own name. From cAdvisor: each pod's containers, leaving out the pod-level cgroup, which would count them twice.

targets.expr: sum by (namespace, workload) (sum by (namespace, pod) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{node=~"$node", container!="", container!="POD"}[$__rate_interval])) * on (namespace, pod) group_left (workload) namespace_workload_pod:kube_pod_owner:relabel or label_replace(sum by (namespace, pod) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{node=~"$node", container!="", container!="POD"}[$__rate_interval])) unless on (namespace, pod) namespace_workload_pod:kube_pod_owner:relabel, "workload", "$1", "pod", "(.+)"))

panels.title: Memory by workload
panels.description: Working set per workload, summed over the selected nodes and stacked: the memory the kubelet counts for eviction and the kernel can't reclaim without pressure. Workloads as in the CPU panel.

targets.expr: sum by (namespace, workload) (sum by (namespace, pod) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{node=~"$node", container!="", container!="POD"}) * on (namespace, pod) group_left (workload) namespace_workload_pod:kube_pod_owner:relabel or label_replace(sum by (namespace, pod) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{node=~"$node", container!="", container!="POD"}) unless on (namespace, pod) namespace_workload_pod:kube_pod_owner:relabel, "workload", "$1", "pod", "(.+)"))
